summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY agent with obfuscated self-updating daemon
details: @whalent/agent-core ships a 13 MB obfuscator.io-transformed dist/index.cjs (string-array shuffle, control-flow flattening, _0xNNNN identifiers; ~103k string entries) that bundles ssh2, node-pty, WebSocket handling, child_process.spawn against process.env.SHELL, and loopback references to 127.0.0.1:3389, 127.0.0.1:5900, and 127.0.0.1:5901. Together these compose a network-to-shell dataflow in which a remote peer drives a local PTY/shell and reaches loopback RDP/VNC on the installer's host, giving the remote operator full-host code execution. The README states the package 'is the package replaced by remote daemon upgrades', meaning the running daemon replaces its own code at runtime from a network source; combined with whole-bundle obfuscation, the update transport, endpoints, and integrity checks are not auditable from the shipped artifact, so arbitrary future code can be pushed to every installed host outside npm-registry visibility. A self-labeled 'agent core' does not downgrade this: the behavior is a remote-controlled backdoor with an obfuscated self-update channel, not a legitimate tool acting on operator-chosen external targets.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
